title: Three pillars of object-oriented programming
context: What are the main features of object-oriented programming?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Encapsulation hides an object's state behind methods and checks changes through them. Inheritance lets a class reuse and extend another class. Polymorphism lets code call one method on many types, and the right implementation runs for each object. Abstraction, often listed as a fourth idea, exposes only what callers need. Prefer composition over inheritance when the relation is not a true 'is-a'.

points.title: Encapsulation
points.why: Keeping fields private lets the class keep its invariants.

points.title: Polymorphism
points.why: Callers depend on an interface and work with any implementation.

points.title: Composition
points.why: Inheritance ties a subclass to its parent. Composition is usually easier to change.
